locator.text: Equation (6.31), p. 71, in the statement of Proposition 6.6

evidence: paper: a_{\gamma,m}\,b_{\gamma,m'} \in \begin{cases} \mathsf{W}_{\alpha+\beta}, & m+m' \neq 0,\ \text{with harmonic } m+m', \\ \mathsf{M}_{\alpha+\beta}, & m+m' = 0,\ \text{after temporal cutoff.} \end{cases}

provenance.note: machine audit: worker, gate, reviewer; not confirmed by a human

verdicts.summary: Lean uses a different formula here. Both branches exist, but as class lemmas with no harmonic side condition and no cutoff hypothesis, and the harmonic bookkeeping sits in a different place. `wave_cmul_wave` gives W_α·W_β ⊂ W_{α+β} and `WaveClass.bilinear_mean` (scalar form `wave_cmul_mean`) gives W_α·W_β ⊂ M_{α+β}, each from 0 ≤ P ≤ 1 and ζ ≤ 1 — the first without 'm+m' ≠ 0', the second without 'm+m' = 0' and without any temporal-cutoff hypothesis, because Lean's `MeanClass` is the ζ-weighted derivative bound alone and contains no ∂_θ = 0 or support clause, so the M-branch is proved for every wave product rather than only for the zero-harmonic one. The clause 'with harmonic m+m'' is encoded instead by the grading: `field_mul` makes a product of harmonic fields the convolution product in AddMonoidAlgebra (α → ℂ) ℤ, so harmonics add, and `carrier_add` adds the phase coefficients. The genuinely zero-harmonic statement of the second branch is `angularProduct_mem`: the angular mean (zero harmonic) of a product of two finite harmonic fields with W_α and W_β coefficients lies in M_{α+β}. Exponents α+β agree in every case; the weight improvement from √ζ·P to ζ matches the paper's ζ^{3/2}P_v ≤ √ζ P_v and ζP_v² ≤ ζ on p. 72.
